THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
A memo is filed reporting death of petitioner No.1.
Memo is taken on record.
Petition as against petitioner No.1 stands dismissed as abated.

2. Heard Sri.T.Basavana Gouda, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri.T.Hanumareddy and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondents.
3.

This petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. with the following prayer:
"To quash the entire criminal proceedings in C.C.No.15/2018 with respect to the petitioners concerned, for the offences P/u/s 177, 419, 420, 468 of IPC, on the file of the Senior Civil Judge & JMFC Court, Hagaribommanahalli."

4. Brief facts which are necessary for disposal of the petition are as under:
4.1 A private complaint came to be filed by the second respondent herein under Section 200 of Cr.P.C.
Hussain Peer Sab S/O Late Imamsab vs The State Of Karnataka on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165866064/
3 making allegations against both the petitioners that they have cheated the second respondent.
Second petitioner impersonated second respondent and entered into a sale deed whereby wrongful loss has been caused to second respondent and petitioners stood gained wrongfully and therefore sought for action.
4.2
The said complaint was referred to police under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. for investigation and to file report.

Based on the order of the learned Magistrate, Hagaribommanahalli police registered the case in Crime No.23/2015 on 21.02.2015 for the offence punishable under Sections 177, 419, 420,
182, 200, 203, 468, 471 and 149 of IPC.
4.3 As many as twelve accused persons were named in the complaint and among them petitioners are accused No.1 and 2.
Police after thorough investigation filed charge sheet for the offence punishable under Sections 177, 419, 420 and 468 of IPC against the petitioners herein and nine others.
4.4 The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offences alleged against the petitioners and others and the case is now pending in C.C.No.15/2018.
5. The order of taking cognizance against the petitioners is under challenge before this Court by the petitioners.
6. Sri

.T.Basavana Gouda, learned counsel for the petitioners reiterating the grounds urged in the petition contended that absolutely no allegations are found against the second petitioner herein and therefore sought for quashing of further proceedings as continuation of proceedings against the petitioner would amount abuse of process of Court and sought for allowing the petition.
7.

Per contra, Sri.T.Hanumareddy, learned counsel appearing for second respondent - defacto complainant contended that the investigation agency after thorough investigation has collected such materials which would prima facie establish the aforesaid offences inasmuch as second petitioner who is wife of first petitioner - Hussain Peerasab and others have colluded together and they have concocted the documents and have sold the property which was standing in the name of Mulimani Yamunabee bearing Khata No.1-302 and they have sold the same in favour of other accused persons for a valuable consideration of Rs.88,000/- and the role assigned to the second accused is that she has mispresented herself as Mulimani Yamunabee and therefore sought for rejection of petition.
8.

Learned High Court Government Pleader supports the argument put forth on behalf of respondent No.2.
9.
In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court has perused the material on record meticulously.

10. On such perusal, it is seen that the investigating agency has collected necessary documentary evidence which would prima facie establish the offence alleged against the petitioners in the charge sheet.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the specific case of the investigating officer that investigation revealed that it is the second petitioner who has impersonated Mulimani Yamunabee and sold immovable property belonging to Mulimani Yamunabee to the other accused persons for a valuable consideration.
12. Prima facie materials available on record in the form of charge sheet clearly point out the guilt towards the second petitioner.

13. Whether at all the second petitioner has really impersonated Mulimani Yamunabee resulting in wrongful loss to the legal representatives of Mulimani Yamunabee and also resulting in wrongful gain to the petitioners and other accused persons are all matters to be thrashed out after full fledged trial by the learned Magistrate in the pending trial.
14. It is too premature for this Court to form an opinion that the second petitioner is totally innocent of the offences alleged against the second petitioner.

15. Since the investigating agency has already collected necessary materials in the form of charge sheet, so as to draw a prima facie opinion that it is the second petitioner who has impersonated Mulimani Yamunabee, expressing any opinion by this Court at this stage that too with the limited jurisdiction of Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is impermissible.

16. Accordingly, following order is passed:
ORDER
Criminal petition as against petitioner No.1 stands dismissed as abated.
Criminal petition as against petitioner No.2 is dismissed.
All contentions and defence available to the accused are kept open to be urged during the pending trial.
